original_question: For a fixed integer n at least 2, form the n-ary power sieve by deleting every n-th remaining number, then every n^2-th remaining number, and in general every n^k-th remaining number for k = 1, 2, 3, .... Does this sieve sequence contain infinitely many primes, and also infinitely many composite numbers?
target_in_paper: Item 28) n-ary Power Sieve (generalization, n ≥ 2): the two conjectures that the remaining sequence contains infinitely many primes and infinitely many numbers of the sequence that are not prime. ([paperzz.com](https://paperzz.com/doc/6992817/florentin-smarandache-sequences-of-numbers-involved-in))
correct_elements: Your draft correctly fixes n ≥ 2, describes the iterative deletion pattern n, n^2, n^3, ... on the surviving terms, and asks exactly the two infinitude questions appearing under item 28: prime terms and nonprime terms of the remaining sequence. ([paperzz.com](https://paperzz.com/doc/6992817/florentin-smarandache-sequences-of-numbers-involved-in))
missing_details: The paper names the construction the n-ary Power Sieve and presents it as the general n-analogue of the immediately preceding binary and trinary sieve entries. ([paperzz.com](https://paperzz.com/doc/6992817/florentin-smarandache-sequences-of-numbers-involved-in))

The starting set is the natural numbers 1, 2, 3, ... ; the question is not posed for an arbitrary initial set. ([paperzz.com](https://paperzz.com/doc/6992817/florentin-smarandache-sequences-of-numbers-involved-in))

At each stage one counts anew from 1 in the current remaining sequence before deleting every n^k-th remaining term; this restart-of-counting is part of the paper’s formulation. ([paperzz.com](https://paperzz.com/doc/6992817/florentin-smarandache-sequences-of-numbers-involved-in))

The paper states the problem as two conjectures for every n ≥ 2, not as a single broader invitation to study related sieves. ([paperzz.com](https://paperzz.com/doc/6992817/florentin-smarandache-sequences-of-numbers-involved-in))

The second clause in the paper is phrased as "there are an infinity of numbers of this sequence which are not prime," so a paper-faithful stand-alone version should preserve that wording rather than silently replacing it by "composite." ([paperzz.com](https://paperzz.com/doc/6992817/florentin-smarandache-sequences-of-numbers-involved-in))
refined_question: For each integer n ≥ 2, start with the natural numbers 1, 2, 3, ... . At stage k = 1, 2, 3, ... , recount the current remaining sequence from 1 and delete every n^k-th term. Let S_n denote the remaining sequence after carrying out all stages of this n-ary power sieve. Does S_n contain infinitely many prime numbers, and infinitely many terms that are not prime? ([paperzz.com](https://paperzz.com/doc/6992817/florentin-smarandache-sequences-of-numbers-involved-in))
justification: The draft is aimed at item 28, not at the neighboring binary, trinary, or consecutive-sieve entries: item 28 gives exactly the general n ≥ 2 deletion rule with powers n, n^2, n^3, ... and immediately lists the same two infinitude conjectures. The refinement only restores the paper’s hidden operational detail that counting restarts from 1 at each stage, makes the universal quantifier over n explicit, names the construction, and keeps the paper’s original "not prime" wording. ([paperzz.com](https://paperzz.com/doc/6992817/florentin-smarandache-sequences-of-numbers-involved-in))
